audit_metadata.platform: Helm Sports Labs v3 (Baseball Recruiting + Golf Team Management)

vulnerabilities.title: Golf Tables Completely Unprotected (RLS Disabled)
vulnerabilities.description: Migration 061 and 062 explicitly DISABLED ROW LEVEL SECURITY on all core golf tables with comment 'RLS disabled for development - re-enable in production'. This appears to be running in production with RLS disabled, exposing all golf data to any authenticated user.
vulnerabilities.attack_scenario: Any authenticated user (including baseball coaches/players from completely different sport) can query ALL golf data: SELECT * FROM golf_rounds; returns ALL rounds from ALL teams. SELECT email, phone FROM golf_coaches; harvests ALL coach contact information.
vulnerabilities.proof_of_concept:
-- As User A (baseball player):
SELECT gp.email, gp.phone, gr.total_score, gt.name
FROM golf_players gp
JOIN golf_rounds gr ON gr.player_id = gp.id
JOIN golf_teams gt ON gt.id = gp.team_id
WHERE gp.user_id != auth.uid();
-- Returns EVERYTHING because RLS is DISABLED
vulnerabilities.impact: Complete data breach of golf platform. Cross-team data exposure (Team A can see Team B). Personal information exposure (emails, phones, GPAs). Performance data exposure (scores, stats, patterns). Competitive intelligence leak. GDPR/privacy violation.
vulnerabilities.affected_users: ALL golf users (coaches and players across all teams) + any authenticated user on platform

fix.description: Re-enable RLS on all 10 golf tables and add proper team-scoped policies for SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE operations

vulnerabilities.verification:
-- Should return 0 rows:
SELECT * FROM golf_rounds WHERE player_id NOT IN (SELECT id FROM golf_players WHERE user_id = auth.uid());

vulnerabilities.title: Conversation Participants RLS Disabled (Fixed but Unstable)
vulnerabilities.description: Migration 078 DISABLED RLS on conversation_participants with comment 'Nuclear Option: Drop ALL Policies' to fix recursion issues. While migration 20260108000001 re-enabled it, the history shows the system couldn't maintain stable RLS policies. This indicates potential for future breakage.
vulnerabilities.attack_scenario: When disabled: SELECT cp.conversation_id, cp.user_id, u.email FROM conversation_participants cp JOIN users u ON u.id = cp.user_id WHERE cp.user_id != auth.uid(); reveals who is messaging whom across ALL conversations, enabling network analysis and social engineering.
vulnerabilities.proof_of_concept:
-- Reconstruct messaging graph:
SELECT c.sport, c.team_id, array_agg(u.email) as participants
FROM conversation_participants cp
JOIN users u ON u.id = cp.user_id
JOIN conversations c ON c.id = cp.conversation_id
GROUP BY c.id, c.sport, c.team_id;
vulnerabilities.impact: Privacy violation: see who messages whom. Network analysis: map relationships. Phishing: impersonate participants. Social engineering: exploit communication knowledge.
vulnerabilities.cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

fix.description: Currently fixed but monitor for recursion issues. Policies use simple user_id = auth.uid() checks without JOINs to prevent recursion.
fix.sql:
-- Already fixed in 20260108000001
-- Monitor logs for: ERROR: infinite recursion detected in policy for relation

vulnerabilities.verification: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM conversation_participants WHERE user_id != auth.uid(); -- Should return 0

vulnerabilities.title: Permissive Conversation Creation
vulnerabilities.description: Policy 'Users can create conversations' uses WITH CHECK (true), allowing ANY authenticated user to create conversations without validation. Combined with SECURITY DEFINER function create_conversation_with_participants(), minimal checks exist.
vulnerabilities.attack_scenario: Attacker creates conversation with arbitrary users: SELECT create_conversation_with_participants(ARRAY['victim-coach-id', 'victim-player-id', 'attacker-id']); then monitors messages, injects phishing messages, or impersonates coach.
vulnerabilities.impact: Unauthorized conversation creation. Message injection. Phishing and social engineering. Impersonation attacks. Cross-team/cross-sport privacy breach.

fix.description: Restrict conversation creation to valid messaging matrix. Require creator_id = auth.uid() and add team/sport validation.

vulnerabilities.verification:
-- Try creating conversation for different team (should fail):
INSERT INTO conversations (sport, team_id, creator_id) VALUES ('golf', 'other-team-id', auth.uid());

vulnerabilities.title: Missing Policies on 15 Golf Tables
vulnerabilities.description: These tables have RLS ENABLED but NO POLICIES defined, making them either completely inaccessible (blocks all ops) OR completely open depending on Supabase/Postgres defaults. The behavior is unpredictable and insecure.
vulnerabilities.attack_scenario: If defaults are permissive: SELECT * FROM golf_coach_notes WHERE shared_with_player = false; exposes private coach assessments like 'Player has attitude problems, consider cutting'. SELECT * FROM golf_travel_itineraries; reveals competitor travel plans.
vulnerabilities.proof_of_concept:
-- Test access (behavior depends on defaults):
SELECT title, content, shared_with_player
FROM golf_coach_notes
WHERE coach_id != (SELECT id FROM golf_coaches WHERE user_id = auth.uid());
-- May return other coaches' private notes!
vulnerabilities.impact: Data exposure if defaults permissive. Feature breakage if defaults restrictive. Inconsistent security posture. Unpredictable behavior. Privacy violation (coach notes, travel, documents).
vulnerabilities.migration_introduced: Various migrations created tables without policies

fix.description: Add complete policy sets (SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE) for all 15 tables with proper team scoping
fix.sql:
-- See PART 7 of migration 20260108000002 for complete policies
-- Example for golf_coach_notes:
CREATE POLICY "golf_coach_notes_select_own_coach"
ON golf_coach_notes FOR SELECT TO authenticated
USING (coach_id IN (SELECT id FROM golf_coaches WHERE user_id = auth.uid()));
-- Plus policies for shared_with_player, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE

vulnerabilities.verification:
-- Verify policies exist:
SELECT tablename, COUNT(*) FROM pg_policies
WHERE schemaname = 'public' AND tablename IN ('golf_qualifiers', 'golf_coach_notes', ...)
GROUP BY tablename;

vulnerabilities.title: Complex SECURITY DEFINER Functions Bypass RLS
vulnerabilities.description: 18 SECURITY DEFINER functions bypass RLS to implement complex authorization logic. These functions are difficult to audit, may contain logic errors, and lack comprehensive input validation and logging.
vulnerabilities.attack_scenario: Exploit logic error in can_users_message(): if function doesn't properly validate team membership, attacker (baseball coach) could message golf players. Exploit create_conversation_with_participants(): no team_id validation allows cross-team conversations.
vulnerabilities.impact: Authorization bypass via logic errors. Cross-team data access. Cross-sport data access (baseball ↔ golf). Difficult to audit and maintain. Potential for privilege escalation.

fix.description: Replace SECURITY DEFINER functions with RLS policies where possible. Add comprehensive logging, input validation, and SET search_path = '' to remaining functions.
fix.sql:
-- Add to each SECURITY DEFINER function:
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION can_users_message(...)
LANGUAGE plpgsql
SECURITY DEFINER
SET search_path = ''
AS $$
BEGIN
  -- Add audit logging
  INSERT INTO audit_log (function_name, caller_uid, params, timestamp)
  VALUES ('can_users_message', auth.uid(), json_build_object('sender', sender_uuid, 'recipient', recipient_uuid), NOW());
  
  -- Add input validation
  IF sender_uuid IS NULL OR recipient_uuid IS NULL THEN
    RAISE EXCEPTION 'Invalid parameters';
  END IF;
  
  -- Existing logic...
END;
$$;

vulnerabilities.title: Permissive Policies Using USING (true)
vulnerabilities.description: Multiple tables use USING (true) or WITH CHECK (true) in RLS policies, making data completely public to authenticated users without any scoping.
vulnerabilities.attack_scenario: Harvest ALL coach contact info: SELECT full_name, email_contact, phone FROM coaches; (no restrictions!). Enumerate invite codes: SELECT invite_code FROM team_invitations WHERE is_active = true; then brute force team access. Spam notifications: INSERT INTO golf_calendar_notifications (user_id, message) VALUES ('victim', 'phishing...');
vulnerabilities.impact: Personal information exposure. Spam and phishing. Competitive intelligence. IP theft (ML models in golf_global_patterns). Invite code enumeration for unauthorized team access.
vulnerabilities.cwe: CWE-732: Incorrect Permission Assignment for Critical Resource

fix.description: Replace all USING (true) with proper team/organization/sport scoping

vulnerabilities.verification:
-- Should return 0 rows:
SELECT * FROM coaches WHERE user_id != (SELECT user_id FROM coaches WHERE user_id = auth.uid());

vulnerabilities.title: Coaches Can View All Baseball Players
vulnerabilities.description: Policy 'Coaches can view all players' allows ANY user with role='coach' to see ALL player profiles, regardless of recruiting_activated status or team membership. This violates privacy for committed players and enables recruiting violations.
vulnerabilities.attack_scenario: Coach from School A queries players committed to School B: SELECT first_name, last_name, email, phone, gpa, sat_score, committed_to FROM players WHERE committed_to = 'school-b-id'; then uses contact info for poaching or unsolicited recruitment.
vulnerabilities.proof_of_concept:
-- As coach from School A, see School B's committed players:
SELECT p.first_name, p.last_name, p.email, p.phone, p.exit_velo, c.name as committed_school
FROM players p
JOIN colleges c ON c.id = p.committed_to
WHERE p.committed_to IS NOT NULL
  AND p.committed_to != 'my-school-id'
ORDER BY p.exit_velo DESC;
vulnerabilities.impact: Privacy violation for committed players. Potential NCAA recruiting violations. Competitor intelligence. Unwanted contact and poaching attempts.
vulnerabilities.cwe: CWE-359: Exposure of Private Personal Information

fix.description: Remove overly permissive policy. Keep only recruiting-scoped policy that requires recruiting_activated = true.
fix.sql:
-- Remove overly permissive policy:
DROP POLICY IF EXISTS "Coaches can view all players" ON players;

-- Keep existing recruiting-scoped policy (from migration 048):
-- "Coaches can view recruiting players" already exists with proper restrictions

vulnerabilities.verification:
-- As coach, try viewing committed player with recruiting_activated=false (should fail):
SELECT * FROM players WHERE recruiting_activated = false AND committed_to IS NOT NULL;

vulnerabilities.title: profile_views INSERT Policy Allows Mismatch
vulnerabilities.description: Policy 'Authenticated users can create profile views' allows viewer_id = NULL OR viewer_id = auth.uid(), enabling view count manipulation and anonymous tracking abuse.
vulnerabilities.attack_scenario: Attacker inflates view counts: INSERT INTO profile_views (player_id, viewer_id) SELECT 'target-player-id', NULL FROM generate_series(1, 10000); creates 10k fake views. OR impersonate another user by setting viewer_id != auth.uid() (if NULL check doesn't catch it).
vulnerabilities.proof_of_concept:
-- Inflate view count:
INSERT INTO profile_views (player_id, viewer_id, viewer_type)
VALUES ('target-player-id', NULL, 'college_coach');
-- Repeat 10000 times to inflate analytics
vulnerabilities.impact: Fake view count inflation. Analytics poisoning. Player ranking manipulation. Misleading recruiting metrics.

fix.description: Enforce viewer_id MUST match auth.uid(), remove NULL allowance

vulnerabilities.verification:
-- Try creating view with different viewer_id (should fail):
INSERT INTO profile_views (player_id, viewer_id) VALUES ('player-1', 'other-user-id');

vulnerabilities.title: golf_global_patterns Exposes AI Intellectual Property
vulnerabilities.description: Tables containing CoachHelm AI/ML patterns and calibration data use USING (true), allowing ANY authenticated user to export all patterns and reverse-engineer the AI system.
vulnerabilities.attack_scenario: Competitor creates account, then exports: SELECT pattern_type, conditions, outcome, prevalence, average_impact, metadata FROM golf_global_patterns; and SELECT bucket, prediction_type, actual_accuracy, calibration_error FROM golf_confidence_calibration; then uses data to build competing AI product.
vulnerabilities.impact: Intellectual property theft. Competitor advantage. Loss of competitive moat. R&D investment wasted. Potential patent infringement by competitors.

fix.description: Restrict global patterns and calibration to users with golf profiles only (prevents arbitrary signups for data theft)

vulnerabilities.verification:
-- As user without golf profile, try accessing patterns (should fail):
SELECT * FROM golf_global_patterns;
